title: Transforming the Basis
teaches: A linear transformation is fully defined by where it moves the basis vectors.
visual: The grid warps smoothly. The red i-hat rotates 90 degrees counter-clockwise to point up, and the blue j-hat rotates 90 degrees counter-clockwise to point left. The entire grid stretches and rotates with them, maintaining parallel lines.
narration: A linear transformation reshapes the space itself. Notice how the grid moves rigidly: if we know where i-hat and j-hat land, we know exactly where every other point in the universe goes.

title: Matrix-Vector Multiplication
teaches: Multiplying a matrix by a vector computes the new position using linear combination.
visual: A green point at (2,1) appears. It moves to (-1, 2). An equation appears: [[0, -1], [1, 0]] * [2, 1] = [-1, 2]. The calculation breaks down visually: 2 times the first column plus 1 times the second column equals the final position.
narration: To find where any point goes, we multiply the matrix by its coordinates. This operation is a linear combination: we scale the new basis vectors by the original coordinates and add them together to find the final destination.
